svg.text: Full-size board: 830 holes, rows numbered 1 to 63. Lay it with row 1 at the left and the letters a to e at the bottom. The five holes of one row, above or below the middle gap, are one contact.
If the letters on your board run the other way, go by the picture. Wire colors only tell the wires apart in the picture: any wire will do.
bottom power lines: leave them empty
bottom power lines: leave them empty
top power lines = isolated side: red (+) is +5V_ISO, blue (−) is GND2. Nothing from the Pico goes in here.
top power lines = isolated side: red (+) is +5V_ISO, blue (−) is GND2. Nothing from the Pico goes in here.
pin 1 next to the USB socket, at the bottom
Isolated side (GND2): the two top power lines and everything right of the dashed line. Never join it to the Pico side. Only U3 and U4 sit on both.
Pico, USB socket at the left: pin 1 in c1, pin 20 in c20, pin 21 in h20, pin 40 in h1
across the gap: d24, g24, d26, g26. SW2: d30, g30, d32, g32
the end with two pins together points at the Pico: f35, f36, then f39, f41
4.7 µF: long leg (+) in h35, the other leg in h36
10 µF: long leg (+) in the red line, the other leg in the blue line, at row 43
6N137, notch towards the Pico: pins 1 to 4 in e45 to e48, pins 5 to 8 in f48 to f45
100 nF: h45 and h48. R4, 1 kΩ: red line (at row 47) and i47. R3, 180 Ω: b41 and b46
SN75176BP, notch towards the Pico: pins 1 to 4 in e52 to e55, pins 5 to 8 in f55 to f52
TVS diode P6KE6.8CA, either way round: h57 and blue line. D3, the same part: h59 and blue line
Pico pin 39 (VSYS, 5 V) to U4 pin 1
Pico pin 1 (GP0, the DMX data) to U3 pin 3
U3 pin 6 to U5 pin 4 (the DMX data)
Before you plug the USB cable in
• Chips U3 and U5: the notch points at the Pico. A chip put in backwards can be destroyed.
• U4: the two pins that sit together are at the Pico end. C3 and C4: the long leg is +.
• The buttons only work across the middle gap, as drawn.
• If your power lines have a break in the middle (a gap in the red and blue lines): this plan only uses the right half.
